schema.description: The schema under test, as JS `.with`-chain source (e.g. `S.string.with(S.minLength, 3)`). You write this by hand; `spec check --write` never touches it.

aliases.description: Alternate `.with`-chain sources that must produce a schema equivalent to `schema` - same ts.input/ts.output, jsonSchema, and operations. Checked live (not separately snapshotted) by `spec check`. You write these by hand.

constructionError.description: The error thrown when `ts.schema` is evaluated — a panic at construction, not at operation compile. Filled by `spec check --write`. Omit when the schema constructs.

_skip.description: Why unasserted: parser-only | serializer-only | lossy | not-applicable | todo(#…).

anyOf.description: Explicit opt-out for an unasserted dimension.

input.description: `S.Input<typeof schema>` as a TS type string. Filled by `spec check --write`.

_skip.description: Why unasserted: parser-only | serializer-only | lossy | not-applicable | todo(#…).

anyOf.description: Explicit opt-out for an unasserted dimension.

output.description: `S.Output<typeof schema>` as a TS type string. Filled by `spec check --write`.

anyOf.description: Explicit opt-out for an unasserted dimension.

instantiations.description: TS type-instantiation cost of this schema. Filled by `spec check --write`.

ts.description: The JS `.with`-chain surface: the schema itself, plus its inferred types and instantiation cost.

input.description: S.toInputJSONSchemaOrThrow(schema), as source text, or its conversion error.

fromInputType.description: The type inferred by S.fromJSONSchemaOrThrow(input), only when it differs from ts.input; omit when equal or when input is a conversion error.

output.description: S.toOutputJSONSchemaOrThrow(schema), as source text, or its conversion error.

fromOutputType.description: The type inferred by S.fromJSONSchemaOrThrow(output), only when it differs from ts.output; omit when equal or when output is a conversion error.

input.description: S.toJSONSchema(schema, { target }), as source text, or its conversion error. Only when this side differs from the default after ignoring $schema.

fromInputType.description: The type inferred by S.fromJSONSchemaOrThrow of this dialect's input document, only when it differs from ts.input; omit when equal or when input is a conversion error.

output.description: S.toJSONSchema(S.reverse(schema), { target }), as source text, or its conversion error. Only when this side differs from the default after ignoring $schema.

fromOutputType.description: The type inferred by S.fromJSONSchemaOrThrow of this dialect's output document, only when it differs from ts.output; omit when equal or when output is a conversion error.

draft-2020-12.description: Sparse fields that differ from the default no-options emit after ignoring $schema. Omitted when nothing differs. Filled by `spec check --write`.

input.description: S.toJSONSchema(schema, { target }), as source text, or its conversion error. Only when this side differs from the default after ignoring $schema.

fromInputType.description: The type inferred by S.fromJSONSchemaOrThrow of this dialect's input document, only when it differs from ts.input; omit when equal or when input is a conversion error.

output.description: S.toJSONSchema(S.reverse(schema), { target }), as source text, or its conversion error. Only when this side differs from the default after ignoring $schema.

fromOutputType.description: The type inferred by S.fromJSONSchemaOrThrow of this dialect's output document, only when it differs from ts.output; omit when equal or when output is a conversion error.

openapi-3.0.description: Sparse fields that differ from the default no-options emit after ignoring $schema. Omitted when nothing differs. Filled by `spec check --write`.

jsonSchema.description: The JSON Schema of both directions, as one-line source text, plus any divergent output type inferred by S.fromJSONSchemaOrThrow for each generated document. Matching types are omitted; if a direction can't be represented, no round-trip type is recorded. Dialect keys record only the fields that differ from this default after ignoring $schema. Filled by `spec check --write`.

input.description: `S.isEqualInput(schema)` source, or the name of the shared comparator it is. Only when the two sides differ.

output.description: `S.isEqualOutput(schema)` source, or the name of the shared comparator it is. Only when the two sides differ.

anyOf.description: The two sides' compiled equality, when they differ.

_skip.description: Why unasserted: parser-only | serializer-only | lossy | not-applicable | todo(#…).

anyOf.description: Explicit opt-out for an unasserted dimension.

isEqual.description: The value-equality of this schema, as source text - or `alwaysEqual` / `strictEqual` / `sameValueZeroEqual`, the shared comparators Sury hands back whole rather than compiling, named the way a pass-through operation is `identity`. A bare string when both sides agree, `{input, output}` when they differ. Every example value is run through it - each equal to a freshly built copy of itself, and to another example's value only when the two values really are the same. Filled by `spec check --write`.

schema.description: Zod (v4) schema whose type differs from ts on ≥1 side, e.g. `z.object({...})`.

divergence.description: How the Zod type differs from Sury's, and why. Hand-written.

input.description: Zod's input type, only if it diverges from ts.input (filled by `--write`); omit when equal.

output.description: Zod's output type, only if it diverges from ts.output (filled by `--write`); omit when equal.

anyOf.description: Zod equivalent that infers a different type than Sury; divergent side(s) recorded.

_skip.description: Why unasserted: parser-only | serializer-only | lossy | not-applicable | todo(#…).

anyOf.description: Explicit opt-out for an unasserted dimension.

zod.description: Equivalent Zod (v4) schema. Bare string: inferred types must equal ts.input/ts.output. Object `{schema,divergence,input?,output?}`: differs from ts - divergent side recorded, matching side omitted. `_skip` if Zod can't express it.

vs.description: Cross-library equivalents, type-checked against this spec.

zod.description: What the `vs.zod` equivalent answers, when it disagrees with parse: the value it returns, as source, or the message it rejects with - the two libraries reading the same input differently (coercion, bounds units, format strictness). Filled by `spec check --write`.

divergence.description: A recorded disagreement between parse and the verifiers that re-run this example.

input.description: Source text for the input, e.g. '"hello"'. Hand-written; `spec check --write` fills output/error.

errorConstructor.description: Expected `error.constructor.name` when the message is the platform's (Node 22 vs 24). Filled by `spec check --write` when this key is present.

reason.description: Why the verifiers below read this example differently from parse. Hand-written, never filled by `spec check --write`. Add a `FIXME:` comment too when it is a bug.

check.description: What `assertInput*`/`isInput*`/`makeInput*` answer, when they disagree with parse: `true` when they accept, else the message they reject with. They validate without building an output, so a failure that only arises while building one is invisible to them. Filled by `spec check --write`.

ajv.description: What the recorded `jsonSchema` documents say, when they disagree with parse: `true` when they accept, else the validator's own words, per side. JSON Schema is allowed to describe a WIDER set than the parser (a refinement has no keyword), so only an accepted example is asked. Filled by `spec check --write`.

zod.description: What the `vs.zod` equivalent answers, when it disagrees with parse: the value it returns, as source, or the message it rejects with - the two libraries reading the same input differently (coercion, bounds units, format strictness). Filled by `spec check --write`.

divergence.description: A recorded disagreement between parse and the verifiers that re-run this example.

additionalProperties.description: A named example: input plus expected output, error message, or error constructor.

examples.description: Named example cases, keyed by a short name (e.g. `valid`, `invalid-type`).

anyOf.description: Compiled codegen plus its runnable examples.

creationError.description: The Sury error thrown when this operation is compiled (a conversion rejected at operation creation). Filled by `spec check --write`.

anyOf.description: An operation that can't be compiled - the creation-time error, ratcheted like codegen.

is.description: unknown → boolean (`S.isInput`). Optional — add when the boolean target's handling is what the spec is pinning.

operations.description: The three compiled directions through the schema (parse, decode, encode), plus optional `assert` and `is`.

description: One schema's complete, machine-checked contract. See the `spec` skill.
